runs.name: Forum Energy Technologies, Inc.; NYSE and NYSE Texas FET, a manufacturer of engineered capital equipment and consumable products for oil, gas, defense and renewable energy in two segments, Drilling and Completions and Artificial Lift and Downhole; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since 2025-01; Variperm bought 2024; NOV, SLB and Tenaris read as the first three named filing rivals
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$77.11** (2026-10-15, the quote printed by `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged; the company's own buybacks at an average $59.79 in April 2026 and $50.77 in June 2026). Shares **11,246,295**, one class (10-Q cover, 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-31, 0001401257-26-000053; issued 13,507,226 less treasury 2,244,808 = 11,262,418 at 2026-06-30, about 16 thousand bought back after; the S-3ASR and 424B7 of 2026-08-28 register 237,552 shares for resale by a selling stockholder, no change to the count; `tools/run.py` used the older 11.304M); cap **$867.2M**; net debt **$110.0M** at 2026-06-30, including $100M of 10.50% bonds due 2029. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001401257-26-000015), 10-Q Q2 2026, DEF 14A 2026 (0001401257-26-000021), 10-Ks FY2024, FY2023, FY2021, FY2020, the 8-K list since 2023-06; one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $70,402 thousand, 10-K cash-flow table, against XBRL). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. Competitors: the 10-K names six rivals, all SEC filers; the first three in its order taken (NOV, SLB, Tenaris), a CONVENTION of the run. Revenue $1,739.7M (2014), $587.6M (2016), $1,064.2M (2018), $512.5M (2020), $791.5M (2025), losses in every downturn. Owner cash after stock pay, capital spending and finance-lease principal averaged $13.2M a year over 2021 to 2025 before purchases, -$17.9M after. Balance sheets 2017 to 2026-06 read: equity $1,409M to $291M, retained earnings $439M to -$844M, goodwill $755M to nil, long-term debt $399M (2019) to $135M, inventory 54% of revenue (2017) to 30% (2025). Q1 IN (revenue "highly correlated to the global drilling rig count" in the filer's words, about 80% consumables and activity-based equipment, the economics readable). **Q2 OUT**: the castle open on the filer's own evidence: rivals "with lower structural costs", larger rivals pressing for "pricing concessions", customers who are competitors and have ceased buying, most valves made by outside manufacturing partners; goodwill written off $961M across 2015 to 2019, Coiled Tubing intangibles $119.1M in 2024; Artificial Lift and Downhole decides at 70.9% of 2023 to 2025 segment profit, pre-tax return on gross segment assets 13.2% (2024) and 11.7% (2025), 9.6% and 7.7% after a share of corporate cost, its predecessor segments losing money in 2020 and 2021; Variperm bought 2024 for $199.0M ($150M cash and 2.0M shares). Field over 2015 to 2025: operating margin FET -18.7%, NOV -10.3%, SLB 0.8% (pre-tax), Tenaris 15.0%; average return on equity -18.9%, -9.4%, -0.8%, 8.9%; FET lowest on every measure. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the proxy features "$80 million of free cash flow" with $14.6M of sale-leaseback proceeds added to operating cash; leverage quoted on adjusted EBITDA; half of long-term pay on relative shareholder return, some units vesting on stock-price thresholds; the proxy letter opening on a 139% stock-price rise; asbestos claims against one subsidiary. After the stop: $1,208M paid for businesses net of sales 2011 to 2025; capital spending below depreciation; buildings sold and leased back ($20.3M 2024, $14.6M 2025). COMPUTATION beneath the stop: cycle base 2016 to 2020 trough to trough inclusive (specific (a), the filer calling 2021 depressed; inclusive a CONVENTION of the run), no organic growth reported so no growth credited (the serial-acquirer pair falling to the no-growth case), no interest shield (a CONVENTION of the run); value **$22.15** a share all-equity, a single point, against $77.11, the plain 2021 to 2025 average giving $48.88 beside; return at the price 2.0% to 3.7%, no case earning the floor; fair price **$7.56 all-equity**, equity-only negative; not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: the SCHYY commit subjects in its opening context, two other companies' research-folder names (AYI, ARCB) in git status, the queue lines of the memory index, the lock file's name; one listing of `Test Runs/` filtered to the run date that returned nothing; none concerns FET. Commits e4a382bb, 7ffcf127, 5d09aa51, 06ee1634, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for FET or Forum Energy). Citations: the analyst's `check_citations.py` PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 29 quoted cites, no missing id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the parts test on a filer that re-segmented in 2024 and recast only 2023, so fewer than five years exist on the present basis; (2) the serial-acquirer convention when the filer reports no organic growth, which made the range one point; (3) trough to trough, whether both end troughs count; (4) whether a part's full-cycle record may be assembled from predecessor segments. Could not get: an organic growth figure, 2021 and 2022 segment figures on the present basis, segment liabilities, the paid-in-kind interest of 2021 to 2023.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: the castle open on the filer's own evidence (rivals with lower structural costs, larger rivals pressing for pricing concessions, customers who are competitors); $961M of goodwill written off 2015 to 2019; Artificial Lift and Downhole decides at 70.9% of 2023 to 2025 segment profit, its best years ordinary returns (13.2% and 11.7% pre-tax on gross segment assets); operating margin 2015 to 2025 -18.7% against NOV -10.3%, SLB 0.8%, Tenaris 15.0%, lowest on every measure. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: free cash flow featured with sale-leaseback proceeds, adjusted EBITDA leverage, pay on relative return. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $22.15 all-equity (no-growth case alone, 2016 to 2020 base) against $77.11, fair $7.56 all-equity, equity-only negative, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: a re-segmented filer in the parts test; no organic growth filed under the serial-acquirer convention; trough-to-trough inclusion.
